title: Continuous cochains form a delta-functor
statement: Let $G$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group and $A$ a finite ring. Let $\mathcal C$ be the abelian category of left $A$-modules with $A$-linear $G$-action and open stabilizers [lem-exc-discrete-modules-abelian]. There is a functor $F:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(A\text{-Mod},\mathbb N)$ whose degree-$n$ term is naturally linearly equivalent to $\operatorname{Cont}(G^n,M)$, with $M$ discrete. Its coefficient maps are postcomposition by equivariant linear maps. Its differential is $d^0m(g)=gm-m$ and $d^nf(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^jf(g_1,\ldots,g_jg_{j+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n)$. There is a cohomological delta-functor $T$ [def-weil-pbc-delta-functor] with $T^q=F\circ H^q$ in every degree. No effaceability or derived-invariants comparison is asserted.

proof.text: Apply continuousCochains_shortExact to the split short exact sequence M --id--> M --> 0, separately for each coefficient object M. Its first complex and term equivalences supply the model K(M), e(M,n), and the differential formula; no separate bar-differential cancellation lemma is needed. Define the coefficient map in degree n by conjugating continuous postcomposition with e(M,n) and e(N,n). Equivariance, additivity and preservation of finite sums show that these maps commute with the differential. The term equivalences prove the identity and composition laws pointwise.

For the chosen abelian structure, the underlying-module functor preserves zero maps and finite limits by discreteModules_abelian. Hence it is additive by Mathlib Functor.additive_of_preserves_binary_products. Evaluating its map_add identity shows that coefficient addition is pointwise addition of underlying linear maps. Conjugating continuous postcomposition therefore proves additivity of the cochain functor.

For an arbitrary short exact coefficient sequence, use continuousCochains_shortExact again. In each degree n, compose its term equivalences with the inverses of e(M,n) to obtain a short-complex isomorphism from its degree-n sequence to the degree-n sequence of the cochain functor. The postcomposition identities prove both commutative squares pointwise. Transfer short exactness along this isomorphism and apply the degreewise criterion for short exactness of complexes. The two zero-morphism instances on the coefficient category are identified by uniqueness of zero morphisms.

Take homology degree by degree. The homology functors are additive, and the homology long exact sequence supplies the connecting maps and its three exactness positions. Degree zero has no incoming differential, so Mathlib HomologicalComplex.mono_homologyMap_of_mono_of_not_rel gives the initial monomorphism from the degree-zero mono. Apply connecting-map naturality to the image under the cochain functor of every short-complex morphism. These are precisely all fields of CohomologicalDeltaFunctor.
